mathgap.title: Signed Difference Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Interpret any phrase of the form “the difference between the number of X and Y” as the signed subtraction X − Y, preserving the order of the names as they appear. This yields a possibly negative value that must be used directly in equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement mentions “difference between the number of X and Y” (including inside difference‑equality statements).
mathgap.example: Treating “the difference between the number of A and B” as |A − B| (absolute value) instead of A − B.

mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate statements like “A has N more than B” (including combined forms) into the equation A = B + N, without imposing any extra positivity constraint beyond the equation itself.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement explicitly says “A has N more than B” or a similar phrasing.
mathgap.example: Assuming A > B must hold and discarding solutions where A − B is negative.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: When a direct count statement “A has N items” appears, set A’s current count to N at that moment, but allow later statements (e.g., transfers) to modify that count.
mathgap.example: Treating a direct count as immutable and refusing to apply later transfers that change the count.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process the problem statements sequentially; as soon as a transfer (or any modification) is encountered, apply it immediately before evaluating any later statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever the problem contains transfer statements.
mathgap.example: Delaying all transfers until after processing every relational statement, thereby ignoring the order of events.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For statements equating one difference to another, such as “the number of X that A has more than B equals the difference between C and D”, translate to the equation (A − B) = (C − D). Keep all four terms; do not drop any side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement equates a directed difference to another difference.
mathgap.example: Interpreting the equality as A = C − D and ignoring B, thereby losing a variable.

mathgap.title: Redistribution to Equal Amount
mathgap.principle: When a group redistributes items so that each member ends up with the same amount, compute the total items, divide by the number of members, and set each member’s count to that integer value (ensuring divisibility).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement describes equal redistribution among a group of persons.
mathgap.example: Computing the new amount incorrectly by forgetting to include all members or by ignoring integer‑division constraints.

mathgap.title: Switch (Swap)
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two persons “switch” their items, exchange their current counts without altering the total number of items.
mathgap.example: Adding the two counts together instead of swapping them.

mathgap.title: Transfer Application (including conditional)
mathgap.principle: For an unconditional transfer “X gives N to Y”, subtract N from X’s current count and add N to Y’s current count immediately; for conditional transfers, apply the same update only if the condition holds.
mathgap.example: Failing to subtract from the giver or to add to the receiver when processing a transfer.

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person “eats N” of an item, subtract N from their current count; when a statement says a person multiplies their items by a factor, multiply their count accordingly.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a modification statement (eating, multiplying, etc.) appears.
mathgap.example: Multiplying the count incorrectly or forgetting to subtract when a person eats items.

mathgap.title: Temporal Snapshot for Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Treat each relational statement as a constraint on the counts at the moment it appears; do not later replace variables in that equation with values changed by subsequent transfers.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a relational statement precedes a transfer involving any of its referenced persons.
mathgap.example: Using a person’s post‑transfer count in an earlier equation that was stated before the transfer.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to interpreting “difference” as a magnitude rather than preserving order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two names and treat the phrase as X − Y, allowing negative results.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements have been processed.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as static constraints and solves the system globally, ignoring temporal order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process statements in the given order, applying each transfer immediately when encountered.

mathgap.description: Assuming ‘A has N more than B’ forces A > B and discarding solutions where A − B is negative.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Misinterpretation that “more” implies a positive difference beyond the equation itself.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate the phrase directly to A = B + N without imposing extra sign constraints.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts are final and immutable.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow later statements (e.g., transfers) to modify counts set by direct assignments.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Simplifying the equation incorrectly by dropping one side of the equality.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the full equality (A − B) = (C − D) and keep all four variables in the equation.

mathgap.description: Applying later transfers retroactively to earlier relational equations.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model solves the whole system at once and forgets that earlier equations should be frozen before later updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Freeze relational constraints at the moment they appear; subsequent transfers affect only later statements.
